defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Only the front candidate observation is available and it visually matches the supplied reference, but the articulated object cannot be fully verified within the remaining budget.

The acquired front rest, mid, and limit observations show no clear mismatch against the compatible reference states, but the full articulated object and configured constraints were not completely verified.

Front-view candidate observations at joint_1 zero and mid are incompatible with the matching reference states: the reference remains straight/horizontal while the candidate visibly tilts and bends the downstream links, indicating an incorrect joint_1 axis.

teacher_findings.description: At joint_1 detents zero and mid the candidate distal links tilt and bend out of the straight horizontal front-view profile, whereas the compatible reference states keep the bar straight and horizontal.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 rotation axis so its actuation matches the reference in-plane horizontal motion instead of producing out-of-plane rotation/bending.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The front-view articulation protocol was observed for rest, joint_0, and joint_1; joint_0 appears consistent, but joint_1 mid/limit motion deviates from the compatible reference states.

teacher_findings.description: In the front view, joint_1 mid and limit poses do not reproduce the reference left-side upper protrusion sweep; the limit pose shows a stepped/top-shifted extension instead of the reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis and anchor so the driven link sweeps outward at the same upper-left location as the reference.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Rest pose matches the reference, but the candidate's joint_0 actuation at zero and mid produces out-of-plane tilting inconsistent with the compatible front reference states, indicating a joint axis mismatch.

teacher_findings.description: With the camera fixed at front, actuating joint_0 to zero and mid swings the link out of the front plane (tilted/foreshortened, oblique-looking silhouettes), whereas the matching reference front zero/mid states remain front-facing with in-plane silhouette changes. The rest pose matches, so the discrepancy appears only under joint rotation, indicating the joint rotation axis does not match the reference.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Realign the joint_0 rotation axis so the link rotates in the same plane/direction as the reference front zero/mid/limit sequence.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The acquired evidence is insufficient to verify the full articulated object.

joint_0 motion matches the reference (rest/mid/limit), but joint_1 produces a clearly different articulation: the candidate tilts and bends the distal links in-plane at mid/limit while the reference keeps the front silhouette horizontal. This is a joint_1 axis mismatch.

teacher_findings.description: With joint_0 returned to rest and the camera in the front view, actuating joint_1 to mid (step 5) tilts the distal links in the image plane, and to limit (step 6) bends the right portion sharply downward. The matching reference states (front, joint_1 mid/limit with the other joint at rest) keep the bar silhouette horizontal and only reveal surface holes/end features, indicating roll/slide about the bar axis rather than in-plane rotation. The candidate joint_1 therefore rotates about an incorrect axis.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis (and confirm its type/range) so actuation rolls or slides the link along the bar's longitudinal axis as in the reference, preserving the horizontal front silhouette instead of pitching/bending the distal links downward.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: joint_0 tracked the reference rest/mid/limit sequence, but joint_1 shows compressed travel: mid produces no visible displacement and limit only reaches a mid-like pose, failing the reference articulation for that joint.

teacher_findings.description: joint_1 articulation is attenuated relative to the front-view reference: at the mid detent (step 4, value 0.22) the candidate remains essentially at the rest silhouette, and at the limit detent (step 5, value 0.44) the upper-left extension resembles the reference mid pose rather than the larger reference limit pose. joint_0 matched its rest/mid/limit references, so the mismatch is specific to joint_1.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Restore joint_1's effective range/scale so that the mid detent produces the reference mid displacement and the limit detent reaches the full reference limit displacement.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate rest pose is compatible, but the actuated front-view sequence does not follow the reference joint motion, indicating a joint-axis mismatch.

teacher_findings.description: The front-view sweep at zero, mid, and limit shows the articulated link rotating out of the reference plane; by the limit detent the panel remains angled instead of matching the front-facing reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Realign joint_0 so link_0 rotates about the reference axis and matches the front-view zero/mid/limit poses.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Front-view candidate observations under joint_1 actuation are incompatible with the matching reference states: the candidate produces a large swinging/bending motion of link_1 while the reference remains straight. Evidence is sufficient to fail the verified scope for joint_1 kinematics.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 swings link_1 into a large out-of-plane rotation (mid pose bends the right end downward ~90 degrees; limit folds it back), whereas the comparable front-view reference for joint_1 at mid/limit keeps the assembly essentially straight and horizontal with only a small axial extension. The candidate joint_1 rotation axis therefore differs from the reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis (and verify its range) so link_1 moves in the same plane/direction as the reference front-view joint_1 protocol.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Front-view rest and actuated poses for joint_0 (mid/limit/rest) and joint_1 (limit) are visually consistent with the compatible reference states, and hierarchy confirms joint_0 carries link_0 while joint_1 carries link_1, but the evidence is insufficient to verify the full articulated object.
The candidate fails the articulated motion check for joint_0 despite matching the rest appearance.

teacher_findings.description: From the persistent front view, joint_0 motion does not reproduce the reference detent sequence: the limit and zero poses place link_0 in a swung/edge-biased orientation rather than the corresponding frontal reference poses, while rest only matches before actuation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_0 axis/anchor so link_0 rotates through the same front-view zero, mid, and limit poses as the reference.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate front-view observations at rest, joint_0 mid, and joint_0 limit are visually consistent with the matching reference states, and the joint actuated and persisted (rest to value 0.01 at mid to 0.02 at limit) without an observed mismatch. However the configured runtime budgets and full object coverage were not established within the exhausted budget.
The front rest, midpoint, and upper-limit observations show no established mismatch with the compatible reference poses, but the evidence is insufficient for full verification.

The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 references reasonably, but joint_1 at the mid detent produces a clearly incompatible bent/downward-curved front silhouette versus the straight reference bar, indicating an incorrect joint_1 axis.

teacher_findings.description: At the front view with joint_0 at rest and joint_1 actuated to mid, the candidate's distal links bend/droop dramatically downward out of the bar plane, whereas the compatible reference (front, joint_1 mid) remains a straight horizontal bar. The joint_1 motion rotates about an incorrect axis, producing an out-of-plane silhouette not present in the reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis so its rotation stays in the bar plane and matches the reference straight-bar motion across zero/mid/limit.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 front references, but joint_1 motion is inconsistent with the corresponding reference states.

teacher_findings.description: For joint_1 at zero, mid, and limit, the front-view candidate does not follow the reference articulation: instead of the reference straight bar/end-feature progression, the candidate shows tilted, downward-curving, and irregular end motion.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct joint_1's axis/anchor so link_1 and link_2 articulate in the same front-plane motion as the reference.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 front-view protocol, but joint_1 motion is inconsistent with the compatible reference states.

teacher_findings.description: In the front view, joint_1 articulation does not match the reference: at mid the expected upper-left protrusion is essentially absent, and at limit the moved geometry appears shifted toward the top rather than matching the reference upper-left extension.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis/pivot so its mid and limit motion reproduce the reference front-view articulation.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The acquired front-view rest/zero/mid/limit sequence is sufficient to show a kinematic mismatch despite matching commanded detent values.

teacher_findings.description: At the zero and limit detents the front-view candidate pose does not match the corresponding reference articulation: the moving link appears tilted/edge-on rather than rotating about the reference vertical joint axis, while the rest pose matches.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Reorient the joint_0 rotation axis/anchor so the actuated link follows the reference front-view motion at zero, mid, and limit detents.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The rest front view is compatible, but the actuated zero, mid, and limit states show link_0 moving out of plane instead of matching the reference front-view rotation protocol, indicating an incorrect joint_0 axis.

teacher_findings.description: With the camera held at front, actuating joint_0 through zero, mid, and limit swings link_0 out of the front/image plane, producing oblique foreshortening and visible depth, whereas the matching reference detents rotate the link within the image plane with no out-of-plane tilt.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Reorient joint_0's axis to the front-view normal so link_0 rotates in the image plane across zero, mid, and limit, matching the reference articulation.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Front-view candidate renders at rest, mid, and limit are visually consistent with the compatible front reference states, and the queried hierarchy contains base, link_1, joint_0, and link_0, but the explicitly stated verification scope is not fully covered.
The acquired evidence is insufficient to verify the full articulated object.

The candidate matches the reference for rest and joint_0 actuation, but joint_1 actuation produces visibly different motion (whole-link tilt/bend) versus the reference, indicating an incorrect joint_1 axis.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 tilts/rotates the downstream links in the front view (notably at zero and mid detents the bar slopes or bends instead of staying horizontal), while the reference joint_1 states keep the bar horizontal with only local right-end feature changes. joint_0 motion matches its reference, isolating the discrepancy to joint_1.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis (and anchor if needed) so its rotation produces the reference in-plane end motion rather than tipping the link chain.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 front-view states, but joint_1 motion is decisively inconsistent with the reference protocol.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 through zero/mid/limit makes the distal links bend or swing out of the straight front-view bar pose, while the matching reference states remain collinear with only the expected end-feature changes.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis and anchor so link_1 and link_0 stay aligned with the reference front-view articulation across zero, mid, and limit.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: joint_0 rest/mid/limit observations are consistent with the reference, but joint_1 mid/limit observations do not match the comparable front-view reference articulation, indicating a joint_1 kinematic defect.

teacher_findings.description: In the front view, actuating joint_1 to mid (step 5) shows little to no upper-side protrusion, and at limit (step 6) the extension appears at the top edge rather than as the upper-side tab seen in the matching joint_1 mid/limit reference states. The link_1 motion therefore differs from the reference articulation while joint_0 motion matches.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis/pivot so link_1 sweeps outward to form the upper-side tab shown in the reference instead of displacing the top edge.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Rest and joint_0 articulation match the front reference sequence, but joint_1 articulation does not: step 5 (mid) shows no visible deflection and step 6 (limit) shows a differently located protrusion compared with the compatible front references.

teacher_findings.description: Observed motion differs from the reference articulation. At joint_1 mid the candidate front view remains a plain rectangle with no left protrusion, whereas the compatible reference shows a clear upper-left protrusion; at joint_1 limit the protrusion appears at the top edge rather than the reference upper-side location.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint axis to match the reference motion.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The rest front view matches the reference, but the joint_0 articulation at zero, mid, and limit does not match the corresponding reference front states, indicating a kinematic defect in link_0's rotation.

teacher_findings.description: In the front view, the reference brings link_0 to a front-facing rectangular orientation at the zero and limit detents (images 1 and 3), while the candidate keeps link_0 oblique/tilted and on the wrong side at the same detents (steps 2-4). The articulation does not reproduce the reference motion for joint_0.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_0 axis/anchor so link_0 rotates into the same front-facing poses as the reference at the zero, mid, and limit detents.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 front protocol, but joint_1 mid/limit motion is inconsistent with the reference.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 to mid and limit produces a large out-of-plane bend/curl of the carried chain, while the compatible front reference states remain essentially straight with only end-detail changes.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct joint_1's axis/anchor so link_1 follows the reference articulation for the mid and limit detents.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The rest pose and joint_0 front-view protocol are consistent, but the joint_1 protocol shows a clear articulation-axis mismatch.

teacher_findings.description: With joint_0 at rest, actuating joint_1 through zero/mid/limit makes the carried link_1 assembly leave the straight front-view reference path: it appears skewed at zero, strongly bent downward at mid, and kinked upward at limit rather than matching the reference joint_1 articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct joint_1's axis so link_1 follows the reference front-view motion, then re-check zero, mid, and limit against the compatible reference images.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Rest and joint_0 front-view motion match the reference protocol, but joint_1 mid/limit observations are inconsistent with the corresponding reference states, indicating a wrong joint_1 axis for link_1.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 does not reproduce the reference front-view articulation: at mid the candidate shows essentially no lateral protrusion where the reference shows a clear upper-side step, and at limit the candidate displaces the top of the bar leftward instead of forming the reference upper-mid side protrusion. The carried link_1 therefore rotates about an incorrect axis.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 rotation axis so link_1 swings laterally in the front plane, matching the reference mid and limit protrusion location and growth.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The front-view articulation protocol (rest, joint_0 mid/limit, joint_1 mid/limit) was observed and is broadly consistent with the reference states, and the hierarchy and reported joint values are coherent, so no front-view kinematic defect is supported. However verification was limited to the single front reference view and the runtime budget constraints were not checked.
The candidate matches at rest but its joint_0 motion diverges from the reference across zero, mid, and limit detents.

teacher_findings.description: With the front camera persisted and only joint_0 actuated, the rest pose matches, but the zero/mid/limit detents produce oblique/out-of-plane silhouettes that do not match the corresponding frontal reference motion.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_0 axis so link_0 rotates in the same plane/direction as the reference articulation.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Candidate observations match the supplied front and oblique_fr reference states across rest, mid, and limit for joint_0, but the verification scope is not fully closed.

No defect is evident in the comparable front and oblique_fr rest/mid/limit observations, and the joint returned to rest, but the evidence is not sufficient to verify the full articulated object and configured constraints.

Candidate observations cover the full reference protocol (front and oblique_fr views across rest plus joint_0 and joint_1 at zero/mid/limit detents) and visually match the corresponding reference states; reported joint values are consistent and render times are nominal.

Front and oblique_fr rest/mid/limit observations for joint_0 and joint_1 were acquired and appear broadly consistent with the reference motion protocol, but the evidence is not sufficient to verify the full articulated candidate.
The candidate matches rest and joint_0 motion, but joint_1 mid/limit states are inconsistent across both compatible front and oblique_fr comparisons.

teacher_findings.description: joint_1 does not reproduce the reference articulation: at mid and limit the upper link fails to extend laterally as in the front and oblique_fr references, and at limit it shows only a small top/axial offset instead of the expected upper side protrusion. joint_0 motion matches its reference states.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct joint_1 axis/anchor so the upper link rotates outward in the same lateral direction and amplitude as the reference while keeping other joints at rest.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Candidate imagery across the front and oblique_fr rest/zero/mid/limit protocol appears consistent with the supplied reference motion, with no clear kinematic or structural defect visible.

Comparable front and oblique_fr observations at matching detents show the candidate articulating about a misaligned joint axis: the upright member tilts and the links open/splay at the extremes, unlike the reference motion.

teacher_findings.description: During the joint_0 sweep the candidate's central post tilts and the two links splay apart instead of rotating cleanly about the reference's upright hinge axis. At the zero detent (front) the post leans off-vertical versus the upright reference, and at the limit detent (oblique_fr) the half-disc separates from the plate rather than closing to the reference edge-on configuration.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Realign joint_0's rotation axis to the reference vertical hinge so the post stays upright and link_0/link_1 rotate together without separation across zero, mid, and limit.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Front and oblique_fr candidate views at rest/mid/limit visually match the corresponding reference states, the joint_0 values are consistent (rest 0, mid 0.01, limit 0.02) with no visible deviation, and the hierarchy contains base, link_1, joint_0, and link_0 in a plausible parent chain. No geometry, structure, or kinematics defect is evidenced. However, the configured runtime budgets (max_triangles/max_draw_calls) were never measured because the stats runtime property was not queried, so the full stated scope is not confirmed.

The acquired front and oblique_fr observations across rest, mid, and limit are visually consistent with the supplied reference motion protocol, and the hierarchy includes the expected parts and joint. However, the configured runtime budget constraints were not measured.

The sampled front and oblique_fr observations across joint_0 and joint_1 at zero/mid/limit/rest are visually consistent with the corresponding reference states, joint values are internally consistent (midpoints match limit averages), and the hierarchy shows a coherent base->link_2->joint_1->link_1->joint_0->link_0 chain with no observed kinematic or structural discrepancy. However the configured runtime budgets and several views/material properties were never inspected, so full verification cannot be certified.

The candidate cleanly matched all comparable reference states: hierarchy is consistent (base -> link_2 -> joint_0/link_0 and joint_1/link_1), front and oblique_fr views at rest plus joint_0 and joint_1 at mid/limit reproduce the reference protrusion pattern (joint_0 lower-left, joint_1 upper-left), and reported joint values are internally consistent (mid equals half of limit for both joints). No defect was observed in the checked articulation. However, the full configured scope was not verified.
The candidate matches rest and joint_0 articulation, but joint_1 motion is inconsistent with the reference in both front and oblique comparisons.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 does not reproduce the reference upper-side protrusion: at mid it is largely absent and at limit it appears as a top/offset block in front and oblique views, indicating an incorrect joint axis or anchor for link_1.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct joint_1's rotation axis and anchor so link_1 swings out to the upper-left as in the reference mid and limit states.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The full student-visible motion protocol was executed and observed: front and oblique_fr views at rest/zero/mid/limit (steps 1-9) match the corresponding reference states, with the rest pose reproduced identically (steps 1 and 5). Hierarchy (step 0) is a valid single-joint chain base -> link_1 -> joint_0 -> link_0, and the joint values are internally consistent (mid 0.26075 equals the mean of zero -0.25133 and limit 0.77283). No kinematic, structural, or geometric discrepancy is evident in any comparable reference/observation pair, and the simple asset renders in ~0.2 ms, comfortably within the configured budgets.
The candidate rest pose matches, but the joint_1 limit observation visibly departs from the compatible reference state, indicating an incorrect joint_1 axis.

teacher_findings.description: In the front view with joint_1 driven to its limit, the candidate's carried link articulation at the right end is skewed/edge-on and does not reproduce the compatible reference limit pose.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 rotation axis so link_1 follows the reference front-view limit motion.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Rest pose and joint_0 motion match the front references, but joint_1/link_1 motion differs from the compatible reference states at both mid and limit.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_1 does not reproduce the compatible front-view reference motion: at mid the expected upper-left protrusion of link_1 is absent (the bar stays plain), and at limit the protrusion appears at the top rather than the upper-side location shown in the reference, indicating link_1 rotates about an incorrect axis.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 rotation axis so link_1 swings outward to match the reference articulation.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The rest front view matches the reference, but actuating joint_0 to its limit produces a visibly different link_0 orientation from the compatible front/limit reference, indicating an incorrect joint axis.

teacher_findings.description: At the joint_0 limit detent with the front camera, the candidate shows link_0 rotated into an angled/edge-on orientation, whereas the compatible front/limit reference shows the panel face-on; the motion path of link_0 does not match the reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_0 rotation axis (and sign) so link_0 reaches the same face-on limit pose as the reference from the front view.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: Front-view candidate observations at rest, mid, and limit show no clear visible mismatch with the compatible reference states, and the reported hierarchy matches the expected joint structure.
The candidate matches the rest and joint_0 front-view protocol, but joint_1 motion is inconsistent with the compatible reference states.

teacher_findings.description: For joint_1 detents zero, mid, and limit, the candidate front-view motion visibly departs from the compatible references: the link bends/rotates into sloped or downward-curved configurations and shows extra articulated artifacts instead of the reference joint_1 poses.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis so link_1 follows the reference front-view articulation for zero, mid, and limit detents.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches rest and joint_0 front-view references, but joint_1 shows a clear incompatible motion at both checked detents.

teacher_findings.description: For joint_1, the candidate front-view motion does not match the compatible reference states: at mid the expected link_1 protrusion is absent, and at limit it appears shifted toward the top rather than the reference upper-left side motion.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_1 axis so link_1 follows the reference front-view articulation at mid and limit detents.

defect_episodes.teacher_summary: The candidate matches at rest, but the joint_0 detent sequence does not reproduce the reference articulation.

teacher_findings.description: Actuating joint_0 to zero, mid, and limit produces front-view motion that visibly departs from the compatible reference detents; the moving link swings/twists out of the expected plane rather than matching the reference articulation.
teacher_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the joint_0 axis so link_0 follows the reference front-view motion across the zero, mid, and limit detents.
